subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should browser tool defaults move to compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals, or should OpenClaw keep capped snapshots with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with existing full snapshot workflows, so automation should not choose the default contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change reports the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access for workflows that need it.

options.title: Keep capped snapshots
options.body: Retain the current AI snapshot caps and opt-in efficient mode, treating browser-specific compaction as targeted follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to broader compaction
options.body: Handle this through the broader context/tool-output compaction architecture instead of changing browser defaults first.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change reports the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access for workflows that need it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser tool and docs history points to this person for the product-boundary choice around browser model-facing semantics.
